 Darryn Peterson, Josh Okogie, Josh Green, Ace Bailey and Jaxson Hayes will start Tuesday’s game against the Heat. 
 With Keyonte George (ankle) sidelined, the Jazz are shifting Peterson into the starting point guard role. That should raise his ceiling considerably. Replacing George in the starting lineup is Okogie, who will be more valuable to the Jazz than to fantasy managers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard

 Keyonte George (ankle) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Heat. 
 George sprained his right ankle during Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves and did not return. His absence means the Jazz will have to rely more on Darryn Peterson and Isaiah Collier. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson exploded for a season-high 26 points (11-of-21 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and one steal over 35 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Peterson, the second-overall pick from last year’s NBA Draft, shot 50 percent from three-point range, burying a season-high four triples in his best offensive performance of his young career. The 19-year-old prodigy possesses a virtually unlimited ceiling from a talent standpoint, but fantasy managers should expect some inconsistency as he acclimates to playing at the highest level. It’s worth noting that he could see an uptick in usage if Keyonte George winds up missing time after exiting this contest with a right ankle injury. The Jazz have lost eight consecutive games and are just 1-9 overall this season. They have a four-game week on tap that features challenging showdowns against the Heat, Magic, Rockets and Spurs. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George (ankle) will not return to Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 George sprained his right ankle early in the third quarter and has since returned to the locker room. With their starting point guard done for the night, the Jazz will rely more on Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 George is now questionable after not appearing on Utah’s initial injury report. If he can’t play, Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson stand to gain the most in playmaking responsibilities. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson filled up the stat sheet with 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, two steals, three blocks, and three 3-pointers on Friday. 
 Peterson got more aggressive in the second half, and the offense started to get going again in the second half because of him. This is the type of game that people were hoping for when the Jazz drafted him 2 nd overall in last year’s draft. He looked more confident and got to the line for six free throws. Granted, four of them were because the Jazz were in the bonus, but its still good to see the defensive stats in this game. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson had 7 points (2-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, and seven assists on Wednesday against the Pelicans. 
 While this wasn’t an amazing game from Darryn Peterson, he is getting prioritized more. The main difference now is that he’s now running as the backup point guard instead of Isaiah Collier which has really helped Darryn’s assist numbers. This is great for Darryn in dynasty if you have him, because that is the skill that he needs to work on for him to develop into a high-level fantasy player. In redraft leagues, he’s worth a stream if you’re looking for points and some assists, but not more than that. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darry Peterson recorded 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Peterson has scored in double figures in each of Utah’s last three games. Against the Trail Blazers, he wasn’t at his best, committing three turnovers, but the rookie guard still finished with a full stat line. Peterson played the entire fourth quarter, sharing the court with Keyonte George (8/3/4/1) for seven minutes and Isaiah Collier (8/1/4/2) for the other five. According to Cleaning the Glass, Peterson has played 90% of his minutes at shooting guard thus far. That split appears unlikely to change anytime soon, which may lower his fantasy ceiling. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson put up 18 points (4-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in an overtime loss to the Spurs. 
 Obviously you want Darryn to be more efficient from the field, but he got his shot attempts up which is what you want to see. He did leave the game in the first quarter with a head injury but returned. He did not close the game which is notable. He will continue to get better, and this is a good game all things considered, but the fantasy upside for this season isn’t very high. 
 Jaxson Hayes 
 UTA 
 Center-Forward 
 #11 
 Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is out for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 After starting Utah’s season opener, Hayes has come off the bench in each of the last two games. His absence could give Josh Okogie and Kyle Filipowski additional rotation minutes, with the latter picking up a DNP-CD on Sunday. Neither is worth streaming. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson scores 15 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds and a three in 30 minutes. 
 After a rough debut, Darryn was more aggressive with his shot and played better. However, the rest of his game was rather empty. He will need to be better than that, and he will in time. For now, unless you need some scoring, there’s not a ton of reasons to have him other than a streamer in most redraft leagues.

 Jalen Green recorded 13 points (5-of-7 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Green has struggled mightily to begin the season, but Tuesday’s performance may have been a step in the right direction. His three three-pointers were a season high and a much-needed performance for a player who began Tuesday shooting 6-of-29 from beyond the arc. Green is still rostered in 72 percent of Yahoo leagues, and Tuesday’s performance may convince some managers to hold onto him for a little longer.

 While Booker wasn’t as prolific scoring-wise as he was in Monday’s loss to the Spurs, the Suns didn’t need him to be. Phoenix’s bench was outstanding against the Clippers, with five reserves hitting double figures. The only issue for Booker on Tuesday was the four turnovers, but he’s been one of the few bright spots for the Suns this season.

 LeBron James amassed 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 James, who was inadvertently raked across the face by Paul George early in the fourth quarter, struggled against the Celtics. The good news for fantasy managers is that he committed just one turnover, but the 41-year-old shot the ball poorly. James, who entered Tuesday’s game shooting 25 percent from three, made just one of six three-point attempts. With the 76ers counting on Tyrese Maxey to be their lead scoring option, James’ ability to hit perimeter shots takes on added importance, and he’s struggling right now.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Joel Embiid (foot) recorded 16 points (2-of-9 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Given the current state of Philadelphia’s center rotation, it’s been tough for Embiid to get the break he clearly needs. The former MVP has been playing through a left foot issue that he appeared to aggravate during the third quarter. And if not for an 11-of-13 night at the foul line, Embiid’s final stat line would have looked a lot worse. After Thursday’s game against the Raptors, the 76ers have a back-to-back on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Pacers before visiting the Nets. That could be a spot where the 76ers look to rest Embiid, if possible.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaylen Brown accounted for 13 points (4-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Much was made of the showdown between Brown and Jayson Tatum, the first time the former teammates would face off in a regular-season game. JB struggled, landing in foul trouble in the first half and never really finding an offensive groove. Brown finished with a complete stat line, but four turnovers did fantasy managers no favors. He’ll look to bounce back on Thursday when the 76ers face the Raptors.
 -  Raphielle Johnson
